import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_15/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_15/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_15/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source0 and Source2 on movie_id
# This join will produce a table with movie info and ratings by user
joined_0_2 = pd.merge(source0, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source1 on user_id to get gender info
joined_all = pd.merge(joined_0_2, source1[['user_id', 'gender']], on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by title and compute average rating filtered by gender
# For gender 'F' and 'M' separately
agg = joined_all.groupby('title').apply(
    lambda df: pd.Series({
        'F': df.loc[df['gender'] == 'F', 'rating'].mean(),
        'M': df.loc[df['gender'] == 'M', 'rating'].mean()
    })
).reset_index()

# Ensure columns have correct types: title (string), F (float), M (float)
agg['title'] = agg['title'].astype(str)
agg['F'] = agg['F'].astype(float)
agg['M'] = agg['M'].astype(float)

# Save the result to the target path
agg.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_15/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_15/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_15/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_15/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_15_2 and Source3_15_1 on user_id to get gender info for each rating
joined_0 = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_15_0 on movie_id to get movie titles
joined_1 = pd.merge(source0, joined_0, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Filter ratings by gender and compute average rating per title for each gender
# Use groupby on title (string, leftmost column in target schema)
# Aggregations: avg rating filtered by gender='F' as F, avg rating filtered by gender='M' as M

# Create separate columns for ratings by gender
joined_1['rating_F'] = joined_1.apply(lambda row: row['rating'] if row['gender'] == 'F' else None, axis=1)
joined_1['rating_M'] = joined_1.apply(lambda row: row['rating'] if row['gender'] == 'M' else None, axis=1)

# Group by title and aggregate
result = joined_1.groupby('title').agg(
    F = ('rating_F', 'mean'),
    M = ('rating_M', 'mean')
).reset_index()

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_15/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
